name: Basra Reed Warbler
rangeDescription: Southern iraq (tigris and euphrates valleys); winters kenya to malawi
description: Medium-sized Acrocephalus warbler with cold gray-olive-brown plumage and whitish underparts. Note the long and slender bill and the short eyebrow that reaches just behind the eye.

name: White-fronted Falconet
rangeDescription: Forest of northern borneo
description: Tiny, compact, black-and-white falcon. Black above, with a white chest and pale orangish belly.

name: Garden Emerald
rangeDescription: Pacific slope of southwestern costa rica and panama; coiba and pearl islands
description: Small hummingbird with limited range. Male entirely glittering green with dark forked tail.

name: Nihoa Finch
rangeDescription: Nihoa island (northwestern hawaiian islands)
description: A finch-billed Hawaiian honeycreeper endemic to the island of Nihoa; does not occur on the main Hawaiian Islands. Unlikely to be confused with any other species; the only other passerine bird on Nihoa is the Millerbird, which lacks the Nihoa Finch’s heavy bill.

name: Planalto Slaty-Antshrike
rangeDescription: Plateau region of central and eastern brazil
description: Small antshrike found in the lower and middle levels of dry forests and at the edge of humid forests. Males are gray overall with a black crown, and white-spotted black wings and tail.

name: Mexican Sheartail
rangeDescription: Hills of barranca de naolinco, central veracruz (east-central mexico), and disjunctly in coastal thornscrub and gardens of northwestern to north-central yucatán peninsula (southeastern mexico)
description: Only in Mexico. Fairly common small hummingbird of dry coastal scrub in northern Yucatan Peninsula; also very local in dry scrub of central Veracruz.

name: Kofiau Paradise-Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Kofiau (raja ampat islands, off western new guinea)
description: A long-tailed kingfisher of lowland forest on Kofiau Island. Dark blue upperparts with pale blue crown and shoulder, red bill, white underparts, rump and completely white tail, shorter and thicker than similar species.
imageCreditName: Keith Valentine I Rockjumper Birding Tours

name: Campbell's Fairywren
rangeDescription: Southeastern new guinea (middle strickland river and mount bosavi area)
description: A small, little-known bird limited to lowland and foothill treefall gap regrowth in southwestern Papua New Guinea. Underparts and long, thick eyebrow pale blue.

name: Biak Coucal
rangeDescription: Biak (cenderawasih bay, off northwestern new guinea)
description: A poorly known, mid-sized coucal endemic to Biak island. All black plumage, distinctive yellow iris, straightish bill and a fierce-looking face.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Blue-backed Tanager
rangeDescription: Eastern venezuela to the guianas and adjacent northeastern brazil
description: Large, striking tanager of tall rainforest. Combination of size and blue-and-yellow plumage is diagnostic; female is more extensively yellow below, including on face.

name: Scaly-throated Honeyguide
rangeDescription: Savanna and riparian woodland of eastern and southern africa
description: Large honeyguide with a finely-spotted throat and streaky breast. Large white patches at the base of the outer tail are conspicuous in flight.

name: Least Storm-Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeds islands off baja california; ranges southward to far northern peru
description: Very small, all-dark storm-petrel with a fairly short, graduated tail. Fairly common and can be seen from shore in the Gulf of California and along the Pacific coast.

name: African Skimmer
rangeDescription: Major rivers, lakes, and coasts of sub-saharan africa
description: Distinctive tern-like bird with long wings, a short tail, and a bizarre bill in which the upper mandible is shorter than the lower mandible. In slow flight, shows a very white underwing and a white stripe along the back of the upperwing.

name: Beck's Petrel
rangeDescription: Breeding sites unknown (new ireland?); ranges to bismarck archipelago and solomon islands
description: A mostly dark-brown petrel with a white underbody and a strongly hooded appearance. Very similar to the larger Tahiti Petrel, but has a smaller, thinner bill and more rounded wings.

name: Black-bellied Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Montane forest of central costa rica and far western panama
description: Distinctive small hummingbird. Male has mostly black body and bright white outer tail feathers, a combination unlike any other hummingbird species.

name: Lesser Yellowlegs
rangeDescription: Alaska and canada; winters to tierra del fuego and galapagos
description: Medium-sized shorebird with bright yellow legs. Plumage is essentially identical to Greater Yellowlegs: gray upperparts with white speckling, streaky neck, and white belly.

name: Grande Comore Brush-Warbler
rangeDescription: Forest undergrowth of grand comoro island
description: A robust, medium-sized brown bird with a long, spiky tail. Endemic to the island of Grand Comoro.

name: Pennant-winged Nightjar
rangeDescription: Brachystegia woodland of southern africa
description: Breeding males have extraordinary “pennants” growing out of their wings. Non-breeding males are still distinctive due to the huge white patches on the wings.

name: Mayotte Sunbird
rangeDescription: Mayotte island (comoros)
description: A small sunbird with a relatively short, slightly downcurved bill. Males are a beautiful mix of green, purple, red, and yellow.

name: Capped Heron
rangeDescription: Lowlands of eastern panama to the guianas, brazil, and northern paraguay
description: This gorgeous medium-sized heron is uncommon but widespread in lowlands of South America, barely extending into eastern Panama. Not likely to be mistaken: combination of silvery back, buffy neck and belly, black cap, and blue lores (sometimes radiant turquoise!) help distinguish this species from other herons.
